title: Zelensky dismisses Zaluzhnyi and appoints Syrskyi as Ukraine's commander-in-chief
body:
On 8 February 2024 Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed decrees changing the leadership of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Presidential Decree No. 59/2024 dismissed Valerii Zaluzhnyi from the post of Commander-in-Chief, and Decree No. 60/2024 appointed Colonel General Oleksandr Syrskyi in his place. Ukrainska Pravda published the report on the decrees at 20:52 on 8 February.

Earlier that day, Zelensky and Zaluzhnyi had each reported on a joint meeting at which changes to the leadership of the Armed Forces were discussed. Mykhailo Podoliak, an adviser to the head of the Presidential Office, said that one reason for the dismissal was the need to review military tactics and prevent stagnation at the front.

Ukrainska Pravda noted that there had been repeated speculation about a possible dismissal of Zaluzhnyi before the decrees were signed. The text of the first decree states that Valerii Zaluzhnyi shall be dismissed as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. The change took place about two weeks before the second anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion on 24 February 2024. Syrskyi's first major decision as commander-in-chief, the withdrawal from Avdiivka, followed on 17 February.
